headline: US bans DeepSeek AI in federal agencies
dek: Homeland Security cites the risk of sensitive data reaching China and blocks new purchases.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Removal order
body: DHS ordered civilian federal agencies to remove DeepSeek products from their IT systems (Convergência Digital, Olhar Digital).
The order also bars new purchases from the company and third-party services built on its technology, per Olhar Digital.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: The risks cited
s3.body: According to Olhar Digital, DHS points to:

points.t: Risk of sensitive data reaching China (Olhar Digital).
Intelligence on citizens and on agencies.
Possible malicious software and flaws, DHS says.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: A ring already closing
body: According to Olhar Digital, the Commerce Department and the Navy had already banned DeepSeek on official devices.
States such as New York, Tennessee and Virginia took similar steps, per Olhar Digital.

stat.cap: states with similar steps, Olhar Digital says

items.t: DHS set no deadline for removing the systems.
China's embassy had not commented, Olhar Digital says.
The order relies on a supply chain security law.

caption.hook: The US told federal agencies to remove DeepSeek AI from their systems and barred new purchases.
body: According to Convergência Digital and Olhar Digital, Homeland Security ordered the removal of DeepSeek products and barred third-party services built on the Chinese company's technology. The department cites the risk of sensitive data reaching China.

Olhar Digital notes that the Commerce Department and the Navy had already banned the tool, as had states such as New York, Tennessee and Virginia. DHS set no deadline for removal, and China's embassy had not commented.
